answer: Every token a key earns carries a short provenance tag, like ink from a quill noting where each coin came from. If a key is later proven to be a sybil, its earnings are clawed back, and so is every coin that flowed from it to other keys within ninety days, taken pro rata from their balances. An operator who funnels fake rewards into one clean spending account sees that account drained too, so a willow-thin front gains nothing. The ledger stays crystal clear about where value came from, and fake keys lose their point.
